adjudication_records.issue_text: quarkus/tests/integration/src/test/java/org/keycloak/it/cli/dist/UpdateCommandDistTest.java:48 — Feature-disabled coverage never asserts the new dedicated exit code 4, so the scripting contract can regress while the test passes.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test `testFeatureNotEnabled` at line 48 only asserts the error message but does not verify the exit code is 4 (FEATURE_DISABLED). Looking at the diff, the test uses `@Launch` annotation and calls `cliResult.assertError()` but never checks `cliResult.exitCode()`. The new exit code 4 is defined in CompatibilityResult.java and used in both UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.java via `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)`. This is a legitimate test coverage gap - the exit code contract could regress without the test catching it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: quarkus/tests/integration/src/test/java/org/keycloak/it/cli/dist/UpdateCommandDistTest.java:88 — Incompatible-version coverage checks only error text and leaves the changed recreate exit code 3 completely unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was changed from 4 to 3 in CompatibilityResult.java. The test at line 88 (testWrongVersions) only calls assertError() to check error messages but never verifies the exit code. Since the exit code semantics changed, this is a legitimate gap in test coverage - the test should verify that incompatible versions return exit code 3. This is a real, specific issue grounded in the diff changes.
